Director Chris Columbus said the actor who was originally cast to play Marv, the villain eventually played by Daniel Stern, in “Home Alone” (1990) was “just awful” and the only person he’s ever fired.

But the dissed thespian pushed back at Columbus’ recollection.

On a “Wildmen” podcast this week, Columbus said one actor had a “horrible” screen test with Joe Pesci’s fellow burglar character.

“It’s the only person I ever had to fire,” Columbus recalled.

The director said that when he called the actor, the person knew he was about to get canned. The filmmaker said he tried to placate him by promising they would work together in the future. “What else am I gonna say?” Columbus told the “Wildmen” hosts.

It never happened.

The studio eventually agreed to cast Stern, Columbus’ first choice.

“So then the studio had to not only pay him, then they had to hire Dan Stern,” Columbus said. “Then it cost them a lot more money.”

While Columbus did not name the unfortunate actor, Daniel Roebuck acknowledged to Entertainment Weekly that he was fired from the role and found the filmmaker’s comments “troubling.”

Roebuck, who had previously copped to being cut from the production, disputed Columbus’ claim.

“They did everything they could to get me to quit,” Roebuck told EW. “There was no screen test with Joe Pesci. That never, ever happened, so that’s impossible. I sat with Joe Pesci for one afternoon. What Chris said to me when he fired me was that there was no chemistry. And I reminded him that the characters literally spent a two-page scene together, and after that they were both being hit in the face with nails. So it didn’t really matter what the chemistry was.”

Columbus said he was forced to cast either Stern or Pesci at first because the two together would be too expensive, and he chose Pesci.

Stern and Pesci were memorable as the bumbling bad guys tormented by Macaulay Culkin’s Kevin, who was left behind by his family in the 1990 Christmas classic.

If its any consolation for Roebuck, Columbus didn’t have much regard for a certain future president when he did a cameo in the sequel.

Columbus accused Donald Trump of bullying his way into “Home Alone 2” in a brief scene at the Plaza Hotel, which Trump owned at the time.
